4º de Primaria · Inglés

Food and shopping: some and any

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Vas a una tienda en Inglaterra. Quieres comprar manzanas, pero no sabes cuántas hay. ¿Cómo preguntarías «¿Hay manzanas?»?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Dirías «Are there any apples?». En inglés usamos some en frases afirmativas («There are some apples») y any en negativas y preguntas («There aren't any apples», «Are there any apples?»). Las dos significan «algo de», «algunos».

2

Aprende9 bloques cortos

Food words

Let's review some food: apples, bananas, oranges, tomatoes, carrots, potatoes, eggs, bread (pan), cheese (queso), milk (leche), water, juice (zumo), rice (arroz), pasta, chicken (pollo), fish and meat (carne).

Some food words have a plural with -s: one apple, two apples; one tomato, three tomatoes. Others don't, like bread, milk, rice or water: we can't count them one by one. En castellano: pasa igual en español: no decimos «tres arroces».

A, an or some?

For one thing we can count, we use a or an: a banana, a carrot, an apple, an egg (we use an before a vowel sound: a, e, i, o, u).

For more than one thing, or for things we can't count, we use some: some bananas, some eggs, some bread, some milk. En castellano: some es «unos», «unas» o «un poco de». «I've got some cheese» = «Tengo (un poco de) queso». Muchas veces en español ni lo traducimos.

Some in affirmative sentences

We use some in affirmative sentences (frases afirmativas): «There are some oranges in the fridge», «I've got some sandwiches for the trip», «We need some water».

We also use some when we offer or ask for something politely: «Would you like some cake?» (¿quieres un poco de pastel?), «Can I have some juice, please?». Consejo: en estas preguntas usamos some porque esperamos que la respuesta sea «sí».

Any in negatives and questions

We use any in negative sentences and in questions: «There aren't any bananas» (no hay plátanos), «I haven't got any money» (no tengo dinero), «Is there any milk?», «Are there any eggs?».

Remember the short answers: «Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.», «Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.». En castellano: en las negativas any equivale a «nada de» o «ningún»: «There isn't any bread» = «No hay (nada de) pan».

Containers and quantities

To buy food we often use containers (envases): a bottle of water (una botella de agua), a carton of milk (un brik de leche), a packet of biscuits (un paquete de galletas), a tin of tuna (una lata de atún), a jar of jam (un tarro de mermelada), a bag of potatoes (una bolsa de patatas), a loaf of bread (una barra de pan).

We also use weights: a kilo of apples, half a kilo of cheese. Don't forget the word of in the middle!

At the shop: asking politely

In a shop, the shop assistant (dependiente) says: «Can I help you?» or «What would you like?». You answer: «Can I have a kilo of tomatoes, please?» or «I'd like some bread, please».

At the end you say «That's all, thank you» (eso es todo). En castellano: en inglés es muy importante decir please y thank you. Pedir algo sin «please» suena maleducado, aunque en español a veces digamos solo «Ponme un kilo de tomates».

Vídeo: Grocery shopping children's song · Hooray Kids Songs & Nursery Rhymes (YouTube) · 9,3 millones de visualizaciones

How much is it?

To ask the price, we say: «How much is it?» (¿cuánto es?) for one thing, and «How much are they?» for more than one. The answer: «It's two euros», «They're one euro fifty».

Prices in English: €3.50 is «three euros fifty»; £1.20 is «one pound twenty». En castellano: en inglés los decimales se escriben con punto, no con coma: 2.50, no 2,50. Y el símbolo de la moneda va delante: €5, £5, $5.

Reading: the picnic

Read: «Tomorrow Irene and her friends are going to have a picnic. Irene looks in the kitchen. There's some bread and there are some tomatoes. There's some cheese, but there isn't any ham. There aren't any crisps and there isn't any juice! She writes a shopping list: a packet of ham, two bags of crisps, a bottle of orange juice. At the shop she asks: "How much is it?" "It's six euros forty." "Here you are. Thank you!"»

What is there in the kitchen? What does Irene buy?

Let's practise: the class shop

Turn the classroom into a shop. Some students are shop assistants and others are customers. Make price labels and use toy food or pictures. Each customer has a shopping list and €10 in paper money.

Customer: «Good morning! Have you got any eggs?» Assistant: «Yes, we have. / Sorry, we haven't got any.» Customer: «Can I have some eggs, please? How much are they?». Consejo: recuerda: some para afirmar y pedir; any para preguntar si hay y para decir que no hay.

Lo hacemos juntos

Complete with some or any: «There aren't ___ carrots.»

  1. Es una frase negativa (aren't).
  2. En negativas va any.

Resultado: any.

Ask politely for bread in a shop.

  1. Fórmula: Can I have…, please?
  2. Pan (no contable): some bread.

Resultado: Can I have some bread, please?

Say the price: €4.75.

  1. Primero los euros: four euros.
  2. Luego los céntimos: seventy-five.

Resultado: four euros seventy-five.

Errores típicos

  • Usar some en negativas: «There aren't some eggs» → «any eggs».
  • Usar a con comida no contable: «a bread» → «some bread» o «a loaf of bread».
  • Olvidar of: «a bottle water» → «a bottle of water».
  • Pedir sin please: añade siempre please y thank you.
  • Escribir el precio con coma: «2,50 €» → «€2.50».

Ejercicios

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

  1. Translate: pan, queso, leche, huevos.

    Ver solución
    bread, cheese, milk, eggs.

  2. Complete with a or an: ___ orange, ___ banana.

    Ver solución
    an, a.

  3. Complete: «There are ___ apples in the bag.» (some/any)

    Ver solución
    some.

  4. Complete: «Is there ___ juice?» (some/any)

    Ver solución
    any.

  5. Complete: «We haven't got ___ rice.» (some/any)

    Ver solución
    any.

  6. Translate: un paquete de galletas, una lata de atún.

    Ver solución
    a packet of biscuits, a tin of tuna.

  7. How do you ask the price of one thing?

    Ver solución
    How much is it?

  8. Say the price: €1.20.

    Ver solución
    one euro twenty.

  9. Short answer (no): «Are there any bananas?»

    Ver solución
    No, there aren't.

  10. Write your shopping list for a picnic (4 items).

    Ver solución
    Model answer: a loaf of bread, some cheese, a bottle of water, a bag of apples.

Para familias

  • Escribid juntos la lista de la compra de la semana en inglés.
  • En el súper, que pregunte en inglés el precio de tres productos y lo lea de la etiqueta.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Léxico de alimentos, envases y precios; some y any; fórmulas de cortesía en compras (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria).

  • Tienda de clase con etiquetas de precio y dinero de papel.
  • Inventario de una nevera dibujada: There is some… / There isn't any…
  • Juego de la memoria: «I went to the shop and I bought some…».

Qué vas a aprender

  • Learn food words and containers (a bottle of, a packet of)
  • Use some in affirmative sentences and any in negatives and questions
  • Ask for things in a shop politely
  • Ask and answer about prices with How much is it?

Palabras clave

some · any · a / an · a bottle of · a packet of · How much is it? · Can I have…? · please · shopping list · euros
